hooks.name: Pad_ProcessReport
hooks.about: One pad report into the pad's state (PadState, at pad), each poll, before the tick reads it.

hooks.name: Hero_UpdateMotionInput
hooks.about: The stick read into the hero, early in his update each tick.

hooks.name: Hero_TurnToHeading
hooks.about: Eases the hero's facing toward his move yaw.

hooks.name: Hero_SetPlanarVelocity
hooks.about: The hero's velocity at his ground speed along an angle; an angle above pi means his facing.

hooks.name: FollowCamera_ApplyOverrides
hooks.about: The follow camera's per-tick requests from the hero's state; the camera moby's update calls it before it places the eye.

hooks.name: Hero_AdvanceAnimation
hooks.about: Ratchet's animation moved on by his animation speed, once a tick after his state's update.

hooks.name: Item_Give
hooks.about: Gives the player item id (GiveItem): sets its owned and obtained bytes, shows its banner, gives its starting ammo, marks it bought in the vendor's stock and adds it to the quick select; equip non-zero also puts it in hand. Every item the game gives goes through it but the Persuader's.

hooks.name: Planet_Unlock
hooks.about: Unlocks a planet's coordinates (UnlockPlanet): its flag (one byte per level), the galaxy list, and its banner unless it is the planet the player is on.

hooks.name: Vendor_InitLevelStock
hooks.about: The vendor's stock at each level start (VendorStockLevelInit): gives the Bomb Glove while the player has none, keeps the stock's known items and adds the level's new weapon.

hooks.name: Vendor_BuildItemList
hooks.about: The vendor menu's list (VendorBuildItemList), from the stock and the items owned: each time the menu opens and after each purchase. skip_unflagged leaves out what is for sale (the menu opened from the pause screen).

hooks.name: GoldBolts_CountCollected
hooks.about: The gold bolts collected, at most 40 (count_nonzero_entries_up_to_40): what the pause screen shows; the unspent ones are this less 4 per gold weapon.

hooks.name: Hero_TakeDamage
hooks.about: Takes hit points off the hero's health (Hero_TakeDamage): at most one a call, none for 0, then the HUD's health bank. Every hit the hero takes goes through it but the instant kills (falls, crushers), which set his health to 0.

hooks.name: Moby_GetHitMessage
hooks.about: The hit pending on moby (MobyGetHitMessage): the record of the last hit posted to it (+0x20 the attacker, +0x24 the flags, +0x2C the damage, an f32) when its flags match mask, else 0, dropping the hit unless keep. How the hero and every enemy read the hits they take, each tick, so a hit may be read more than once.

hooks.name: Weapon_TakeAmmo
hooks.about: Takes amount of ammo from item for a shot (TakeAmmo; -1 is the item in hand): 1 when taken, 0 when there is too little. An item with no ammo limit takes none and gives 1.

hooks.name: Moby_RecordDeath
hooks.about: Records a placed moby's death or a crate's break (SetDeathBits): its save id's killed bits (none for a save id below 0), its mission, then drops its bolts: about the s16 at +0xB4 (or what a tallied source has left of +0xB6), which it then clears.

hooks.name: Level_LoadGameplay
hooks.about: Loads a level's gameplay file into the level heap (LoadLevelGameplay), once per level start: the settings, the placed mobys and their pvars, the spare moby pool, the paths and the rest; returns the heap cursor. After it, every placed moby exists and none has run.

hooks.name: Hero_ApproachSpeed
hooks.about: Eases the hero's ground speed (+0x194, the speed Hero_SetPlanarVelocity moves him at) toward his target speed (+0x190) by up when below it and by down when above, each tick he moves on foot, in every level.

hooks.name: Damage_BuildHit
hooks.about: hit_desc_build: fills a hit descriptor (0x24+ bytes) for a hit on an enemy: the 16-byte direction vector at +0, attacker moby +0x10, mask +0x14, damage f32 +0x1c, +0x20 = 1. Every attack that hurts an enemy builds one (the wrench on the stack right before its swing sweep), so a hook that calls the original with another damage changes what is dealt. Checked against the wrench update's call (a0 = descriptor on the stack, a1 = attacker moby, a2 = mask, a3 = vec4 direction, f12 = damage). Every level.

hooks.name: Damage_HitVictim
hooks.about: hit_ring_write: posts a hit descriptor on the victim moby into the 64-entry hit queue at 0x178100 (stride 0x40) unless the victim already holds a stronger hit this tick (victim byte +0xa4 = queue slot); the victim reads it in MobyGetHitMessage (rac1.combat.get_hit). To hurt an enemy from a mod: build a descriptor with omni.with_stack and the build_hit function, then call this. a0 = victim, a1 = descriptor (asm of the prologue). Every level.

hooks.name: Wrench_SwingSweep

Returns 1 when something was hit. Only caller: the class 71 update. Argument registers a0..a3, t0, t1, t2 checked in the caller's asm. Every level.

hooks.name: Ammo_Pickup

hooks.name: Damage_Resolve
hooks.about: The shared hit resolver (Veldin FUN_0025a088, names row hit_knockback): every enemy class calls it once per tick from its prestep with the hit entry that rac1.combat.get_hit returned. a0 = the victim moby, a1 = the hit queue entry (0 = none; +0x20 attacker moby, +0x2c strength), a2 = the victim's component block (pvar +0x20: the health float, +8 the component byte), a3 = 0 in every caller read, t0 = u32 out (status: 0, or 1 = no usable hit), t1 = f32 out (the STRENGTH the class subtracts from its health; may be 0 = no pointer), t2 = u32 out (-1 or untouched, may be 0), t3 = mode (4 = take it from the component byte). The return value is the reaction class (0 nothing, 0xb, 0xd, jump-table cases), NOT the strength: the strength is written to *t1 (= entry +0x2c, which the resolver sets from the attacker table for Blaster classes 0x131 and 0xa8). A mod scales damage dealt to enemies by calling original and then multiplying the f32 at strength_out (when it is not 0) and entry +0x2c; it reads the victim's health first through the pvars/structs (enemy.health). Signature checked in the asm prologue (a0..a3, t0..t3 stored/used) and the Ghidra C (8 parameters) and a caller (toad prestep FUN_002d4b08: a0 victim, a1 entry, a2 pvar+0x20, a3 0, t0 &status, t1 &strength, t2 0, t3 4). Every level.

The held update calls it 2 leading and 2 trailing times per tick. A mod calls original again with its own vel vector (omni.with_stack) for extra flames. Argument registers checked by argscan and the caller at 0x2b7880 (Ghidra C: FUN_0026abc0(float, vec*, vec*, byte)). Every level.

functions.name: create_moby
functions.about: Spawns a moby of class (arg) in the dynamic pool and returns it (0 when the pool is full). Sets the class's update function and a zeroed 0x80-byte pvar; position, rotation and pvar contents are the caller's job (write moby.x/y/z, then the class's pvar). The moby updates from next tick. Only spawn classes that are loaded: the weapon classes 121 bomb, 74 mine, 457 R.Y.N.O. rocket, 186 Doom agent, 172 Visibomb missile, 153 Devastator rocket, 122 spark, 1192 glow sphere, 112 fireball are resident in all 19 levels; a class without updater yields an inert slot.

functions.name: moby_attach_to_joint
functions.about: World matrix of an attach point of a moby's model: (moby, attach index, out). Writes 0x40 bytes to `out` (struct matrix4: three basis rows, translation at +0x30, world space). The attach index picks a joint through the class's attach table (class_ptr+0x1c): for the hero 0 = right hand (weapon grip), 14 = left hand, 12 = right shoulder, 13 = left shoulder. `out` must be game memory (use with_stack(0x40, ...)); the third argument is that address, not a number.

moby.about: A moby record (an object of the level: enemy, crate, weapon projectile, hero), 0x100 bytes; the pointer comes from hooks (victim, owner, ...).

fields.name: x
fields.about: World position, metres (x east-west; proven on the Kerwan fight: victims, projectiles and effect mobys sit within a few metres of the hero's position and move smoothly; y is the same, z is up).

fields.name: y
fields.about: World position y, metres.

fields.name: z
fields.about: World position z (up), metres; a standing enemy has the ground height of the hero's feet.

fields.name: state
fields.about: The class's state number (its update's switch).

fields.name: flags
fields.about: Moby flags: 0x1000 in the target registry, 0x4000 hittable, 0x20 has a component (pvar word 0), 0x10 tint, 0x40 no anim, 0x4 no transform, 0x2 not updated, 0x100 explicit basis (bit 0 and 0x1000 are set/cleared by enemy prestep code).

fields.name: pvar

fields.name: flags_w
fields.about: Writable alias of `flags` (same offset +0x34, same u16). Bits a mod sets: 0x4 = no transform: the moby's update does not rebuild the basis rows (+0xc0/0xd0/0xe0) from rot_x/rot_y/yaw, the rows you write stay; 0x2 = not scheduled: the scheduler skips the moby's update function (the hero's held items are driven by the hero code instead; HeroItemsAttach sets 0x6 on them); 0x8000 = mirror: the basis is left-handed (determinant -1, row 1 negated) and the moby is drawn mirrored (the renderer reads this bit; the Blaster has no one-sided faces, so a mirrored copy does not turn inside out). A mirrored clone uses 0x8000|0x4 (and 0x2 so it runs no update). Other bits drive collision and AI (0x1000 target registry, 0x20 has a component, 0x4000 hittable, 0x100 explicit basis, 0x10 tint, 0x40 no anim, 0x1 hidden): read `flags`, change only your bit, write the whole word. A wrong word can crash the moby's own update.

fields.name: omni.menu.weapons_page.highlight_class
fields.about: Pause menu, Weapons page: the moby class of the 3D model of the highlighted item (overlay global 0x1b9e10 in Veldin, written by the page's item function 0x27b808 when the cursor lands on a weapon; 0xFFFFFFFF = nothing yet; e.g. Bomb Glove 192, item 16 -> 176, item 15 -> 168, item 11 -> 157, item 19 -> 177; it follows the cursor one tick later). Overlay data in the host's overlay window: reads fail outside a level. It is the model class, not the item id: the id is *(u16*)(*(S+0x48) + *(S+0x3c)*10 + 6) with S = *(*(0x1b9cf4)+0x40) (a pointer chain, no plain field).

fields.name: omni.hud.ammo_box.max
fields.about: The HUD ammo box: the maximum it shows right now, the N of the printed "count/N" (element +0x08). The game copies it from the weapon's cap only when the box is created, so after a cap change on the weapon that stays held (a level-up) the box keeps the old N until the weapon is switched or holstered; a mod writes the new cap here (and to def_max) and the box shows it on the next frame. Meaningful only while the box shows (the id field says which weapon it belongs to). Overlay data in the host's overlay window (0x40000000 + the NTSC-U level-0 address, the host maps it to the level now loaded), so a read or write works in a level and fails on the title screen / between levels. Slot 0 of the game's 4-slot HUD element array (stride 0x90; Veldin 0x17dc50) is the ammo box.

fields.name: omni.hud.ammo_box.def_max
fields.about: The HUD ammo box: the maximum the game compares when it re-requests the box every tick (element +0x28). If it differs from the weapon's current cap the game restarts the box (fade out, fade in) to load the new one; write the same value as omni.hud.ammo_box.max so the compare finds an identical request and no restart happens. Overlay data in the host's overlay window (0x40000000 + the NTSC-U level-0 address, the host maps it to the level now loaded), so a read or write works in a level and fails on the title screen / between levels. Slot 0 of the game's 4-slot HUD element array (stride 0x90; Veldin 0x17dc50) is the ammo box.

fields.name: omni.hud.ammo_box.id

Read-only for mods; check it before writing max / def_max. Overlay data in the host's overlay window (0x40000000 + the NTSC-U level-0 address, the host maps it to the level now loaded), so a read or write works in a level and fails on the title screen / between levels. Slot 0 of the game's 4-slot HUD element array (stride 0x90; Veldin 0x17dc50) is the ammo box.

fields.name: omni.hero.health
fields.about: Ratchet's health: the nanotech orbs the HUD shows (1 to omni.hero.max_health; 0 = dead). Hero_TakeDamage takes at most 1 a call; the game sets it to the maximum when a level starts and after a death, a nanotech pickup adds 1 (up to the maximum). A mod may write it (1 .. max while he is alive): the HUD meter shows the new value. Checked on both discs (PAL v1.00 and USA use the same address, 2026-10-25); the pal column is ntsc + 0x100 [?: unverified, the script binding reads the ntsc column on this disc].
